commands.name: agent.attachPreset
commands.summary: Attaches `presets` (library presets; `engram/default` turns the Default slot on) after the `after` preset in call order (else at the end). Applies what it can: each one it cannot attach is in `skipped` with why (`not-found`, `wrong-kind`, `already-present`, `item-path-invalid`). CONFLICT `library-unavailable` (a library preset named while the library cannot be read — with `mount` when that preset's mount cannot be read) · `root-generation-stale` applies nothing.

commands.name: agent.cancelQueuedInput
commands.summary: Cancels one entry of the waiting list (the same command as the ✕ on screen) — `outcome` = `cancelled` (withdrawn right away) | `requested` (a cancel was requested — the list shows the outcome). An id not on the list is NOT_FOUND. CONFLICT = the name is ambiguous (two or more with the same name — point at it by id) or a connected viewer holds this agent's input (try again after it lets go).

commands.name: agent.detachPreset
commands.summary: Detaches `presets` (every attached entry of each; `engram/default` turns the Default slot off — CONFLICT `default-preset-detach` unless `yes`). Detaching what is not attached changes nothing; an entry that is not a library path is matched by its exact text, and one that matches nothing refuses, INVALID_ARGUMENT `item-path-invalid`. CONFLICT `root-generation-stale`.

commands.name: agent.duplicate
commands.summary: Registers a copy of an agent beside it (the same parent), asleep, named after it with the next number (`bob` → `bob(1)`): the same backend, mode, folder, env and presets, with no conversation or history. INVALID_ARGUMENT when this surface does not create the original's backend; CONFLICT at the roster ceiling. After a timeout or an unknown outcome, check `agent.list` before calling again.

commands.name: agent.interrupt
commands.summary: Interrupts the running turn (≠ kill — the process lives). `outcome` = `requested` (the interrupt was sent — whether the turn actually stopped is announced by the turn-end event). NOT_FOUND = no such agent or it is asleep. CONFLICT = the name is ambiguous · there is no turn to interrupt · this agent does not support interrupt · a connected viewer holds this agent's input.

commands.name: agent.list
commands.summary: The whole roster — name · liveness · working folder · parent — and the state of the roster store (`store`).

commands.name: agent.listQueuedInputs
commands.summary: The list of inputs a live agent received mid-turn without confirmation yet that they were accepted (non-terminal only). `state` = `queued` (before confirmation — we hold it or handed it to the agent and wait for the outcome. codex hands it over by steer when the running turn's tool ends, or to the next turn if the turn ends without a tool · claude hands it to the CLI queue right away) | `sent` (codex handed it to the agent and waits for the echo saying it was received — cancelling does not remove it) | `unconfirmed` (handed over but unknown whether it was accepted — it stays on the list and mail waits for that outcome, and cancelling removes it right away · ★no backend emits it today★ — that stage of codex was removed, ADR-0235) | `cancelling` (a cancel was requested — stays until the agent produces an outcome). `cancel.answer` = `none` (no answer yet) | `not_removed` (the agent answered it could not remove it, or the request failed) · `cancel.vendor_closed` = the agent already closed that entry. `stopped_after_error` = the previous turn ended with a real error and no turn has ended successfully since — meanwhile mail does not go in automatically (kernel `last_end_failed`). User text codex holds may go out again the moment new user text comes in (ADR-0235 decision 4). An asleep agent holds no list (NOT_FOUND).

commands.name: agent.move
commands.summary: Changes the parent in the tree.

commands.name: agent.new
commands.summary: Registers a new agent in the roster (does not launch it — it stays asleep). `presets` are judged as `agent.attachPreset` judges them: the agent is created with what can be attached, each one left out is in `skipped` with why. CONFLICT `library-unavailable` (a library preset named while the library cannot be read — with `mount` when that preset's mount cannot be read) or `root-generation-stale` creates nothing.

commands.name: agent.presets
commands.summary: An agent's presets: the Default slot, the attached presets, its working folder and why it is locked, its backend and mode, `base_rev`, and the folders, conflicts, problems and notices a launch would meet — it leaves out the `missing` problem rows (and the `library_unavailable` row of a library mount that is not registered or not there) and refuses on the others.

commands.name: agent.rename
commands.summary: Changes the display name.

commands.name: agent.reorderPresets
commands.summary: Puts the attached presets in `order` — every entry `agent.presets` shows, each once (a duplicate as often as it is attached), else INVALID_ARGUMENT `reorder-order-mismatch` with the expected order in `args`. `base_rev` = the `base_rev` you read; CONFLICT `rev-mismatch` = the attachments changed since (read them again). The Default slot is untouched. CONFLICT `root-generation-stale`.

commands.name: agent.resolve
commands.summary: Resolves 1–8 words pointing at agents (name or id) at once — `agents` is in the same order as the request. The resolving rules are the same as other verbs taking `target` (exact id match first · then exact name match — case-sensitive · asleep agents included). `live` = `state` of `agent.list` is `live`. If even one cannot be resolved, it returns no line and fails. The text of a failure caused by one word always starts with `targets[i]: ` (i = that word's position counting from 0) — INVALID_ARGUMENT = an empty word (only whitespace) · NOT_FOUND = no such agent (the trailing `candidates` of the text = names worth choosing, in name order · `none` if the roster is empty) · CONFLICT = that name exists two or more times (the trailing `candidates` of the text = those ids — call again by id). If the count is outside 1–8, it is INVALID_ARGUMENT without that head.

commands.name: agent.setWorkspace
commands.summary: Changes an agent's working folder. `cwd` must be an existing absolute folder, else INVALID_ARGUMENT `workspace-not-found` {cwd, why} — `why` also says `not absolute`, or that the folder did not answer in time (`timeout`), could not be read, or is on a network share that is not reachable (`share not reachable`). Only an asleep agent that has never conversed can change it: CONFLICT `workspace-locked` {reason: `running` | `preparing` | `conversed` | `changing`}. The agent keeps its name.

commands.name: agent.spawn
commands.summary: Starts an agent: wakes an existing one (`target`) or creates one in `cwd` and starts it. A preset item that is not found, or the items of a library mount that is not registered or not there, do not block: they are left out and named in `notices` (one notice per mount, with `mount`). A blocked launch starts nothing and is `CONFLICT` with `args.reasons`, one row per reason by `kind`: `broken` {kind, item, via, code, args, line?} (a folder entry that cannot be read included) · `conflict` {kind, items: [{item, via}], code, args, line?} · `library_unavailable` {kind, code, args: {mount, message}, line?} (a library mount that exists but cannot be read). Fix the listed items, then start again. With `cwd`, a launch blocked before the agent is added answers `CONFLICT` with `args.reasons` and creates nothing; a start failure after the add is `INTERNAL` with `args.agent_id` (plus `args.reasons` when blocked) — start that agent by target, do not create another.

commands.name: library.addMount
commands.summary: Registers the absolute folder `path` as the mount `name` (`create` makes the folder once the overlap check passed — a refused check creates nothing; no file is copied or moved) and saves it in library.json; answers the status and `already_pointing` — references that already named `name` and now resolve into the folder. The same name already at the same folder only saves again. INVALID_ARGUMENT `mount-name-invalid` (one name: no `/ \ :`, no leading `.`, at most 64 characters, not `engram`) · `item-path-invalid` (a relative path); CONFLICT `mount-name-taken` · `mount-overlaps` (`with` = `mount` + `mount` — another mount's folder, inside or holding it; only mounts are judged) · `library-config-read-only` (nothing done) · `library-root-unusable` (the folder cannot be used, or whether it overlaps could not be told — nothing published) · `library-unavailable` (the run's first overlap check of the saved mounts has not finished — nothing done; repeat the call) · `library-config-write-failed`.

commands.name: library.copy
commands.summary: Copies `paths` into the folder `to_folder` — each keeps its name (a built-in item from `engram` takes its file's name); copied into its own folder it takes the copy name (`a - Copy.md`, then `a - Copy (2).md` …, whatever `on_conflict` says). A taken name follows `on_conflict` (unspecified: that item's `conflict` `name-exists`); a same-name folder is never merged (`copy-merge-refused`). Each copy is made aside under a temp name and then put in place; nothing refers to a copy, so no reference changes. Answers one row per path in the order given; a copy that failed part-way names its staging in `args` (`staging_row` — it went into the trash —, or `staging` · `staging_disk` · `staging_kept` when it stayed). INVALID_ARGUMENT `item-path-invalid` (as `library.move`); CONFLICT `mount-read-only` · `library-unavailable` · `root-generation-stale` (met after copying: `args.args.stagings`). Can take long; after an answer that never came the outcome is unknown — do not repeat; read the destination after a pause.

commands.name: library.delete
commands.summary: Deletes `paths` into each one's own mount's trash (`.trash`, one bundle per mount per call — `library.listTrash` shows it, `library.restore` brings rows back). When preset files or agents refer to what goes, the first call applies nothing and answers CONFLICT `delete-unconfirmed` with `plan` (`presets` — the preset files listing a deleted path —, `agents`), `plan_digest` and `forms`: repeat with `yes` (references kept — they read as not found until a restore) or `yes` + `detach_refs` + that `plan_digest` (their lines and attachments removed). A plan that changed before the repeat answers the same CONFLICT with the fresh plan, nothing applied. Answers one row per path in the order given (`items`), and with `detach_refs` the paths `detached`, the preset files `written` and `skipped` with why, the `agents` changed and `stopped` when that fix stopped part-way (the items stay deleted). CONFLICT `library-unavailable` · `delete-unconfirmed` · `root-generation-stale`, or the agent store's refusal when it is read-only and agents would change. Emptying the trash is not a command of this list.

commands.name: library.emptyTrash
commands.summary: Removes trash rows for good — nothing goes to an OS Recycle Bin: `bundles` empties each bundle of exactly the rows the trash view listed for it (what it did not list stays, with the record), `rows` deletes single rows for good. Answers every addressed row (the bundles' rows in the order given, then `rows`) and every addressed bundle with its outcome; one that is not gone carries why. INVALID_ARGUMENT `nothing-to-empty` (neither `bundles` nor `rows`); CONFLICT `library-unavailable` only from a daemon that runs no library; UNSUPPORTED `shell-only` from any caller but the Engram app. Can take long; after an answer that never came, read the trash view again rather than resend.

commands.name: library.folders
commands.summary: Every folder of the library, flat, by path; a skill folder is marked `skill`, a hook folder `hook`; each mount (a top folder) carries its `state`. The folders of a mount that cannot be read are left out and the mount is named in `unavailable` (the built-in mount `engram` too when its folder cannot be read, though its rows stay as stand-ins and a launch goes on with `builtin-unavailable`). CONFLICT `library-unavailable` when no scan of the library could be applied.

commands.name: library.list
commands.summary: The items directly in `folder` (unspecified = the library's top, which holds only the mounts) and its plain subfolders. `query` searches name and description (case-insensitive) in every item below `folder` and answers matching rows only (no `folders`). `kinds` keeps only those kinds (unspecified or empty = all; a broken file counts as the kind it claims; a skill's `SKILL.md` matches only `SkillFile`, a hook's `hooks.json` only `HookFile`). A `folder` at or below a link answers one `path-through-link` row, which the filters do not apply to. Unspecified `folder` lists the mounts, each with its `state` — the built-in read-only mount `engram` among them (`engram/default`, `engram/priming`, folder `engram/settings`); a `query` without `folder` searches the mounts that can be read and names the others in `unavailable` (the built-in mount `engram` too when its folder cannot be read, though its rows stay as stand-ins and a launch goes on with `builtin-unavailable`). CONFLICT `library-unavailable` (with `mount`) when `folder` is in a mount that cannot be read.

commands.name: library.listTrash
commands.summary: The trash of every registered mount, in mount order: its bundles by id (one per delete per mount), each with when it was deleted and its rows — `original` is where `library.restore` puts a row back and `restorable` says whether it can. A mount whose trash cannot be read is named with its `problem`, not waited for. Reads only. CONFLICT `library-unavailable` only from a daemon that runs no library.

commands.name: library.move
commands.summary: Moves `paths` into the folder `to_folder`, each keeping its name — on one volume a rename that never replaces, across volumes a copy whose original then goes into its own mount's trash. A taken name follows `on_conflict` (unspecified: that item's `conflict` `name-exists`); on one volume same-name folders merge entry by entry, across volumes they are refused (`crosses-volumes`). Every preset file that names a moved path is rewritten whole, then the agents are re-pointed — no confirmation, except when a referenced folder's lone marker (a skill's `SKILL.md`, a hook's `hooks.json`) leaves it, or a merge would leave a referenced skill or hook folder without it (an entry stays behind, the marker would take a keep-both name, or a `hooks.json` would land beside a `SKILL.md`): then nothing is applied and the answer is CONFLICT `hook-unconfirmed` when every folder referred to is a hook, else `skill-unconfirmed`, with `plan` (`presets`, `agents`), `plan_digest` and `forms` — repeat with `yes` (references kept) or `yes` + `detach_refs` + that `plan_digest` (references removed). Answers one row per path in the order given (`items`), the old → new `mapping` the references followed (apply in order), the preset files `written` and `skipped` with why, the git working `trees` they lie in, the `agents` re-pointed, `detached` skill and hook folders, and `stopped` when the reference fix stopped part-way (the items stay moved; `library.relink` the old path once it is cleared). INVALID_ARGUMENT `item-path-invalid` (`to_folder` is no library path or holds a dot or temp name) · `detach-refs-invalid` (`detach_refs` with no such marker or merge); CONFLICT `mount-read-only` (`to_folder` in the built-in mount `engram`) · `library-unavailable` · `skill-unconfirmed` · `hook-unconfirmed` · `root-generation-stale` (an unconfirmed or stale refusal met after copies across volumes also names them in `args.args.stagings`), or the agent store's refusal when it is read-only and agents would change. Can take long (a copy across volumes); after an answer that never came the outcome is unknown — do not repeat; read the destination after a pause.

commands.name: library.newFile
commands.summary: Creates file `name` of `kind` in `folder` (unspecified: refused as `library.newFolder`) from an empty template (`.md` or `.yaml` is added unless the name ends with it); answers its path. Refusals as `library.newFolder`.

commands.name: library.newFolder
commands.summary: Creates folder `name` in `parent` (unspecified: INVALID_ARGUMENT `virtual-root-read-only` — nothing is created at the library's top; a mount's name alone is a parent like any folder); answers its path. CONFLICT `name-exists` (nothing replaced) · `library-unavailable` (with `mount` when the parent's mount cannot be read — nothing is written into it) · `mount-read-only` (`{mount, path}` — the parent is in the built-in mount `engram`) · `root-generation-stale` · `library-write-failed` (a retry after it may answer `name-exists` — the partial file or folder stays); NOT_FOUND `not-found` = the parent is missing.

commands.name: library.read
commands.summary: One item's detail: its row, its file on disk (`absolute`), the presets that list it (`presets_direct`) or reach it through nested presets (`presets_indirect`), the agents that attach it (`agents_direct` — a preset only) or a preset reaching it (`agents_indirect`), an instruction's `excerpt` and a settings file's field names (`settings_fields`). A built-in (`engram/…`) counts only the Default slot: `agents_direct` = the agents whose Default slot is on for `engram/default`, and the preset and indirect lists are empty (every other built-in: all empty). NOT_FOUND `not-found` = no such item (a mount's name is not an item); CONFLICT `library-unavailable` (with `mount` when the item's mount cannot be read).

commands.name: library.refresh
commands.summary: Re-reads `folder` (unspecified = the whole library) from disk and reports it: `changed` items, `problems` of the files re-read, `no_kind` (yaml files with no `kind` — not listed), `skipped_links` (links not entered) and `errors` (where reading failed — those items are kept as they were; a mount that could not be read, or one registered or moved during the scan and so not walked by it, is a row with its name as `path`; a row with no `path` = the folder asked for could not be read — or is in the built-in mount `engram`, which is never scanned). Use it after changing library files outside Engram. It never refuses except for a `folder` that is not a library path (INVALID_ARGUMENT `item-path-invalid`).

commands.name: library.relink
commands.summary: Re-points every reference to `from` (in preset files, then agents) at `to`; when `from` is missing it also re-points the other missing items of `from`'s folder whose names are in `to`'s folder (`more` of them). Answers the pairs `fixed`, the files `written`, the files `skipped` with why, and `stopped` when an IO failure stopped it after a write (run the same relink again once it is cleared). NOT_FOUND `not-found` = `to` is not in the library; INVALID_ARGUMENT `relink-kind-mismatch` = `to` is of another kind than its references need; CONFLICT `library-unavailable` (with `mount` when `to`'s mount cannot be read) · `mount-read-only` (`{mount, path}` — `from` or `to` is in the built-in mount `engram`) · `root-generation-stale`. A file in a mount that cannot be read is not rewritten: it is in `skipped` with `library-unavailable` and its `mount`. A `skipped` row whose `path` is a mount's name means that mount could not be read at all: references inside it may remain (`fixed` covers the mounts that were read) — run the same relink again once it is back.

commands.name: library.relocateMount
commands.summary: Points the mount `mount` at the absolute folder `path` under the same name (`create` makes it first; no file is copied or moved; references do not change) and saves it in library.json; answers the status. Pointing it at the folder it already has only saves again. Refusals as `library.addMount` except `mount-name-taken`, judged against every other mount, plus NOT_FOUND `mount-not-found` and CONFLICT `mount-read-only` (`engram`).

commands.name: library.removeMount
commands.summary: Unregisters the mount `mount` — no file is touched, ever; adding it back restores every reference. Answers the status, `now_absent` — references that name it and now read as absent (a launch skips them with one notice) — and `outcome` = `removed`, or `saved_only` when the mount was already gone because an earlier removal's save failed (only library.json was written). NOT_FOUND `mount-not-found`; CONFLICT `mount-read-only` (`engram`) · `library-config-read-only` · `library-unavailable` (as `library.addMount`) · `library-config-write-failed`; INVALID_ARGUMENT `mount-name-invalid`.

commands.name: library.rename
commands.summary: Renames the item `path` to `name` in its folder (a case-only rename too) — a move to a new name, answered as `library.move` answers (one row): a taken name is the row's `conflict` `name-exists` (nothing replaced), its own spelling is `skipped` `in-place`; references follow, and a referenced skill's `SKILL.md` or hook's `hooks.json` renamed so its folder is no skill or hook asks first (`skill-unconfirmed` or `hook-unconfirmed`, as `library.move`). Refusals as `library.move`, with `name` — not one valid name, or a dot or temp name: INVALID_ARGUMENT `item-path-invalid` — in place of `to_folder`.

commands.name: library.renameMount
commands.summary: Renames the mount `mount` to `to` and re-points every reference to `mount/…` (in the preset files of every mount that can be read, then in agents) at `to/…`; a case-only rename is allowed; saves library.json. When files would be rewritten, or references would stay as they are because their mount cannot be read, the first call applies nothing and answers CONFLICT `mount-rename-unconfirmed` with `plan` (`files` per mount with `git` — the mount is in a git working tree —, `unread` mounts with `paths` — their files that refer to `mount/…` and stay as they are; null: never walked, what in it refers is unknown —, `agents`, `whole_files` — rewritten whole, comments and quoting not kept —, `already_pointing`), `root_generation` and `plan_digest` (over the files in `plan` and its never-walked mounts); repeat with `yes` and that `root_generation` and `plan_digest` — both required whenever the plan needs confirmation: files to rewrite or references left unread (either missing: the same refusal; stale: `root-generation-stale` with a fresh `plan` and `plan_digest`). To have the unread files rewritten too, wait for their mount and call again instead of confirming. A confirmed call whose plan is no longer the one confirmed — a preset came to refer to `mount/…` or stopped, a mount came back or became unreadable — applies nothing and answers `mount-rename-unconfirmed` with the fresh `plan`; read it and confirm again. Answers the status, the pairs `fixed`, the files `written` and `skipped` with why, `stopped` when an IO failure or the agents' save stopped it part-way (the old name stays and the answer carries no `plan_digest` — call again: the repeat plans what is left, and a plan that needs confirmation is answered as above to confirm with its own tokens, while the tokens confirmed before the stop answer `mount-rename-unconfirmed` or `root-generation-stale` with that plan unless it is the confirmed one again — every written file came to refer to `mount/…` again), and `already_pointing` — references that already named `to` (0 for a case-only rename where names ignore case). A `skipped` row whose path is a mount name: that mount was never walked, so what in it refers to `mount/…` is unknown. `git` is null when it could not be told. NOT_FOUND `mount-not-found`; CONFLICT `mount-unusable` (`{mount, state, why}` — the mount cannot be read, so its own references could not be rewritten) · `mount-name-taken` · `mount-read-only` (`engram`) · `library-config-read-only` · `library-unavailable` (as `library.addMount`; also when no first scan of the library could be applied, or a mount's folder — `mount` itself included — was lost during the rename: the old name stays, repeat after `library.status`) · `library-config-write-failed`, or the agent store's refusal when it is read-only and agents would change; INVALID_ARGUMENT `mount-name-invalid`.

commands.name: library.restore
commands.summary: Restores trash `rows` (as `library.listTrash` lists them) to the same paths in the same mounts, making missing parent folders; nothing is ever overwritten — a taken name is that row's `conflict` `name-exists`, and with `keep_both` the row comes back as `name (2)`, `name (3)` … instead. Answers one row per given row in the order given. CONFLICT `library-unavailable` · `root-generation-stale`.

commands.name: library.status
commands.summary: The library's mounts now, in order — each with its `name`, its folder `path`, `default` (at the default place), `builtin` (the read-only mount `engram`, always last) and `state` (+ `state_why`; checked now, the built-in's read at start); `config` (library.json) = `ok` | `read_only` | `corrupt` | `unsaved` (+ `config_why`; `unsaved` = a mount change is live but not saved), `suggested_new` = the default place. `root_generation` = pass it to an edit, which then refuses if a mount changed since (CONFLICT `root-generation-stale`). CONFLICT `library-unavailable` only from a daemon that runs no library.

commands.name: preset.add
commands.summary: Adds `items` (each into the list of its kind, `backend` for all of them) or absolute `folders` — one of the two — after the `after` entry (else at the end). Applies what it can: each item it cannot add is in `skipped` with why (`not-found`, `wrong-kind`, `already-present`, `preset-cycle`, a backend word it does not take …). A bad folder refuses the whole call, INVALID_ARGUMENT `preset-folders-refused` naming each. NOT_FOUND `not-found` = no such preset file; CONFLICT `library-unavailable` · `mount-read-only` · `root-generation-stale` · `library-write-failed`.

commands.name: preset.check
commands.summary: Judges a draft of the preset's lists as `preset.save` would, without writing: the folders it would list, the conflicts and problems a launch of it would meet, and `save_refuses` = a save of this draft would be refused (each mismatch is a `broken` problem with `args` `{path, list}`). `folders` or `hooks` omitted = the file's folders or hooks stay, judged as they are. CONFLICT `library-unavailable` (with `mount` when the preset's mount cannot be read) · `mount-read-only` (a path in the built-in mount `engram`).

commands.name: preset.get
commands.summary: A preset's entries with their state, its folder entries, the conflicts and problems a launch of it alone would meet, its edition `rev` and how many agents attach it. `path` = a library path or `engram/default`. NOT_FOUND `not-found`; INVALID_ARGUMENT `wrong-kind` (not a preset); CONFLICT `library-unavailable` (with `mount` when the preset's mount cannot be read).

commands.name: preset.previewFolder
commands.summary: What a folder entry would load: the absolute `folder` normalized (`path`, `null` = not absolute), why `preset.add` would refuse it (`refused`), and per backend (`backend`, unspecified = every one) and mode (`mode`, unspecified = both) what that backend loads from it. `truncated` = the listing stopped at its cap, `skipped` = entries it could not read, `unlisted` = why a folder that exists could not be listed. Reads only. INVALID_ARGUMENT `backend-tag-unknown`; CONFLICT `library-unavailable` only from a daemon that runs no library.

commands.name: preset.remove
commands.summary: Removes `items` (every entry of each, in every list) or `folders` — one of the two; removing what is not there changes nothing. Answers the preset after the change. NOT_FOUND `not-found` = no such preset file; CONFLICT `library-unavailable` · `mount-read-only` · `root-generation-stale` · `library-write-failed`.

commands.name: preset.reorder
commands.summary: Puts one `section` (`presets` | `instructions` | `skills` | `hooks` | `settings` | `folders` — another word is INVALID_ARGUMENT) in `order` — every entry `preset.get` shows in it, each once (a duplicate as often as it is listed), else INVALID_ARGUMENT `reorder-order-mismatch` with the expected order in `args`. `base_rev` = the `rev` you read; CONFLICT `rev-mismatch` = the file changed since (read it again). NOT_FOUND `not-found`; CONFLICT `library-unavailable` · `mount-read-only` · `root-generation-stale` · `library-write-failed`.

commands.name: preset.save
commands.summary: Replaces the four lists (and `hooks` and `folders`, when given — omitted = they stay) with the draft, all or nothing: any mismatch (not a path, an unknown backend word, one item twice in a list, an item of another kind, a cycle, a relative folder …) refuses the whole save, INVALID_ARGUMENT `preset-save-refused` listing each. A missing item is allowed. `base_rev` (optional) = the `rev` you read; CONFLICT `rev-mismatch` = the file changed since. NOT_FOUND `not-found`; CONFLICT `library-unavailable` · `mount-read-only` · `root-generation-stale` · `library-write-failed`.

commands.name: preset.setBackend
commands.summary: Sets the backend of `items` in instructions, skills and hooks (`backend` unspecified = every backend). Applies what it can: an item the preset does not list, or lists only in presets or settings, is in `skipped`. An unknown backend word refuses the whole call, INVALID_ARGUMENT `backend-tag-unknown`. NOT_FOUND `not-found`; CONFLICT `library-unavailable` · `mount-read-only` · `root-generation-stale` · `library-write-failed`.

commands.name: usage.get
commands.summary: The usage limits of one backend (5-hour · weekly · per-model weekly) — the values the daemon holds. If the next automatic query time has passed, it launches a query here (or attaches to one in progress) and waits up to 5 seconds for it to end — past that it answers with the held value with `in_flight` = true and the query continues. `served` = `Fresh` (a value fetched by the query this request waited for) | `Cached`. `state` = `Ready` | `NotInstalled` | `NeedsLogin` | `Unavailable` (this account has no limit info — no windows are carried) | `Failed` (`next_attempt_in_secs` = until the next automatic query) | `Rejected` (upstream refused — until `retry_in_secs` passes, even `usage.refresh` does not query). Even on failure, the windows are the last known values. The cause of an abnormal state = `detail_kind` (category word) · `detail_code` (the number upstream gave) · `upstream` (upstream original text — secrets masked · 200 chars). A window's `left_pct` = the amount left (`used_pct` is the amount used), and `null` means unknown (not 0). Time fields are relative seconds as of the moment of answering, and only `resets_at` is epoch seconds. A backend whose field this daemon does not hold is NOT_FOUND.

commands.name: usage.refresh
commands.summary: Forces a new query of the usage limits (the same command as ⟳ on screen) — launches a query (or attaches to one in progress) and waits up to 5 seconds for it to end, answering with the same row as `usage.get`. There is no call interval limit — it queries again even if the previous query just ended, and if frequent, upstream may refuse (that refusal may show only as `Failed`, not `Rejected`). Answering with the held value (`Cached`) without querying = the upstream refusal period remains (even if a value came in during the refusal and `state` is `Ready`, the period remains — `retry_in_secs` is not carried then). Even if the query fails or does not end within 5 seconds, it is `Cached` (the query did go out then). The meaning of the fields is the same as `usage.get`. A backend whose field this daemon does not hold is NOT_FOUND.
